references.text: Job describes similar anxiety and unrest, where he lies down asking when he will rise up, and the night becomes long—the same theme of fearful waiting as time passes.
The immediate context describing a trembling heart, failing eyes, and a soul full of longing—the basis for the constant fear described in verse 67.
Lamentations expresses similar despair and anxious waiting, where morning brings longing for evening and evening for morning.
Ecclesiastes describes how the worry of the heart gives no rest at night—the same theme of anxiety that disturbs both day and night.
Isaiah describes the watchman asking during the night, with the same restless waiting and longing for time to pass.
The psalmist describes affliction every morning—the same pattern of daily renewed suffering and fear.
